title: Motion graphics: Lottie, Rive, Spine and DragonBones (assets and runtimes)
description: Vector animation sources and the runtimes that play them. Lottie files from LottieFiles use the Lottie Simple License; Rive community files are CC BY; the Spine runtimes are source-available but need a Spine Editor licence; DragonBones, lottie-web, dotlottie-web, ThorVG and the Rive runtimes are MIT.

items.title: Lottie Simple License (LottieFiles)
items.summary: Licence for free public animations on LottieFiles: copy, modify, publish and distribute, including commercially; modifications stay under the same licence; no compiling files to build a competing service; attribution encouraged, not required.
cautions: Do not bulk-collect LottieFiles animations into a library or service.
The help centre also says not to resell or redistribute the original files as standalone animations.

items.title: LottieFiles help: can free animations be used commercially?
items.summary: Help-centre answer: free animations are under the Lottie Simple License and may be used for commercial business use.

items.title: LottieFiles help: Animation licensing basics
items.summary: Help-centre overview of free versus premium animation licensing; creators may add restrictions on individual animations.
cautions: Read each animation page for creator-specific restrictions.

items.title: LottieFiles help: Commercial use and attribution
items.summary: Help article on commercial use and how to attribute when you choose to (attribution should be visible to end users).

items.title: LottieFiles: Noto animated emoji collection
items.summary: Noto-style animated emoji as Lottie on LottieFiles; third-party packages describe Google's Noto Animated Emoji as CC BY 4.0.
items.licence: CC-BY-4.0 (as reported for Noto Animated Emoji; confirm on the source)
cautions: Licence comes from secondary sources; confirm Google's licence file before use and credit Google Noto.

items.title: Qt docs: Lottie example attribution (Lottie Simple License text)
items.summary: Qt documentation page that reproduces the Lottie Simple License (FL 9.13.21) for an example animation; shows how a product credits a LottieFiles animation.

items.title: airbnb/lottie-web
items.summary: Renders After Effects (Bodymovin) Lottie JSON on the web with SVG, canvas or HTML renderers; MIT. Useful for headless frame capture into video.

items.title: LottieFiles/dotlottie-web
items.summary: Player for Lottie JSON and .lottie (bundled animations, themes, state machines, assets) on a Rust + WASM core powered by ThorVG; MIT.

items.title: Lottie Animation Format specification (lottie-spec)
items.summary: Working-group repository specifying Lottie's JSON structure, semantics and rendering; developed under the Community Specification License 1.0.

items.title: ThorVG vector graphics engine
items.summary: C++ engine rendering SVG (Tiny) and Lottie JSON; MIT. Godot integrates ThorVG for vector UI and assets.

items.title: Rive docs: Community overview
items.summary: Rive community files are shared under CC BY and can be remixed into your own account as a starting point.
items.licence: CC BY (version as shown on each file page)
cautions: CC BY requires credit to the original file's author in your video or credits.
The docs say 'CC BY' without a version on the overview; record the version shown on the file page.

items.title: Rive docs: Marketplace overview
items.summary: Rive Marketplace files are also shared under a CC BY licence.
items.licence: CC BY (version as shown on each file page)
cautions: Credit the author; confirm the CC BY version on the file page.

items.title: rive-app/rive-runtime
items.summary: Low-level C++ Rive runtime and renderer; MIT.

items.title: rive-app/rive-wasm
items.summary: JavaScript/TypeScript + WebAssembly runtime for Rive animations; MIT.

items.title: EsotericSoftware/spine-runtimes (incl. spine-godot)
items.summary: Official Spine runtimes for Godot, Unity, Unreal, web (spine-ts), C/C++ and more. Source is public but NOT open source: integration needs a Spine Editor licence.
cautions: You need a valid Spine Editor licence when you integrate the runtimes, or every user of your product needs one.
The Spine trial licence grants no right to use the runtimes.

items.title: Spine Runtimes License Agreement
items.summary: Terms for the Spine runtimes (updated 2025 on the English site): integration under Section 2 of the Spine Editor License Agreement.

items.title: Spine Editor License Agreement
items.summary: The paid editor licence whose Section 2 permits integrating Spine runtimes into your products.

items.title: DragonBones/DragonBonesJS
items.summary: TypeScript/JavaScript runtime for DragonBones skeletal animation (Egret, PixiJS, Phaser, Hilo, Cocos Creator); MIT. The README points to LoongBones for authoring.
cautions: Older ecosystem: check activity and tooling before building a pipeline on it.
